title: ephemeral-lease-handoff-resume-time-slicing-and-client-checkpointing
author: Priya Menon
description:
Background: We see intermittent availability issues for long-running streaming sessions when clients disconnect briefly (mobile flapping, NAT churn). Existing long-lived leases both tie up worker slots and create noisy reclaim logic. This PR introduces an ephemeral handoff + time-slicing model: short-lived server leases (default 30s) that capture a lightweight session snapshot checkpoint; a resumable client workflow that attempts soft resume using a one-time resume token; and a preemption/time-slice reclaim policy to allow high-priority requests to evict inactive long tails without killing resumable work.

Goals: 1) reduce orphaned GPU slot retention caused by client disconnects, 2) keep tool/function-call idempotency intact across resume, 3) maintain OpenAI-streaming compatibility for clients that expect a continuous SSE/ws stream.

What changed:
- New ephemeral lease controller that issues short TTLe leases and stores compact checkpoints (KV of model position + pending toolcall markers) in in-memory indexed storage with optional persistence to Redis for private deployments.
- Resume token construction: single-use, scope-limited token tied to session id, last-seen token version, and a replay-cap window to prevent double-execution of tool calls. Tokens are intentionally opaque and rotate on every snapshot.
- Client-suggested checkpoint points: clients can request a checkpoint at safe boundaries (post-toolcall, at top-level narrative turns) via a small protocol extension to streaming events; server still snapshots automatically on disconnect.
- Time-slice preemption: long-running sessions paved into 1s slices; if a worker needs capacity, inactive slices are checkpointed and evicted; active slices get grace-run for spans up to a configured soft-run window.
- Backoff and reconnect flow: clients attempting resume follow a hedged strategy (fast rejoin -> bind resume token -> server validates and rehydrates checkpoint) with a short escrow window to accept late rebinds while preventing split-brain.
- OpenAI compat: streaming SSE frame semantics preserved; we add a streaming-control event "x-resume-hint" that falls back to existing behaviors for clients that ignore it.
- Tool/function-call safety: we add per-toolcall confirmation markers in the checkpoint and make tool calls idempotent by replaying only unconfirmed calls on resume.

Tests & rollout:
- Unit tests for checkpoint serialization, token rotation, resume validation, and tool-call replay logic.
- Integration tests that simulate NAT churn, flaky clients, and worker preemption; flaky e2e surfaced once and was rerun in CI.
- Canary rollout toggles: feature gated behind runtime flag that defaults off for older clusters; automatic telemetry captures resume success rate, mismatch errors, and average slot reclaim latency.

Backwards compatibility & migration notes:
- Clients that do not opt into the checkpoint hints will continue to behave as before; they get the server-initiated ephemeral leases but will not benefit from client-initiated lower-latency resumes.
- Resume window configurable per deployment; default conservative values chosen to avoid double-run of toolcalls.

Security: ephemeral resume tokens are HMAC-signed with rotating keys (KMS integration for Private installs).

Privacy: checkpoints avoid storing user prompt text by default; only model position and toolcall metadata are persisted unless customer opts in.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-4907: expose resume metrics in Console and add a retry budget per API-key.
- ENG-4958: opt-in durability tier that persists full snapshots to object store for very long resumes.
